title: ESPRA: ESP32 Speech and Proximity Roaming Assistant
summary: A voice-controlled ESP32-S3 robot that drives, turns toward whoever is speaking, and talks back in under 5 s.
details:
What it is
A voice-controlled desk robot on an ESP32-S3. It wakes when someone sits down, listens hands-free, turns toward whoever is speaking and replies in under 5 s. The whole project is my own, including the Python server.

Speaker buzz
Traced persistent audio buzz to the speaker wiring and rewired the two 4 Ω speakers from parallel (2 Ω, below the MAX98357A's rated load) to series (8 Ω), then capped digital audio at 0.25–0.40 of full scale to stop clipping from the amp's fixed +9 dB gain.

Audio and graphics on two cores
Split audio and graphics across the ESP32-S3's two cores with FreeRTOS, so blocking SSD1309 OLED writes over 400 kHz I2C no longer interrupted the 24 kHz APLL-clocked I2S stream. Zero-filling the DMA buffer stopped pops during redraws, and rate-limiting the mouth animation removed I2C buzz from the speaker leads.

Sensing and voice
Added a VL53L0X ToF sensor that wakes it when someone sits down and dual INMP441 mics for TDOA direction finding, streaming speech to a Python server (Groq Whisper, LLM, Edge-TTS) over 4 KB framed USB serial and later HTTPS, replying in under 5 s.

title: Beehive Winter Monitoring System
summary: Led the electrical design of a ~$200 winter hive monitor, now being installed for UofT BEES.
details:
The monitor
Led the electrical design of a ~$200 winter hive monitor, placing SCD41 CO2 and BME680 sensors in a vented in-hive enclosure and three DS18B20 probes on a shared 1-Wire bus, cabled through IP68 glands to an outdoor ESP32 enclosure uploading data over Wi-Fi every hour.

Keeping the bees safe
Derived a 1.94 V/m E-field exposure limit from a published bee EMF stress study, then used free-space power density and the 377 Ω impedance of free space to calculate an 11.2 cm minimum ESP32 distance at 2 dBm, confirmed by EMF meter readings of ~1 V/m.

Wiring and power
Specified a 2 m shielded 6 × 22 AWG cable rated to −40 °C to carry switched 3.3 V, ground, I2C, and 1-Wire data out of the hive, with the shield grounded at the outdoor end only to avoid a ground loop. Ran the I2C bus at 50 kHz across the 2 m cable, checking that rise time stayed under the 1 µs limit with an estimated ~450 pF of bus capacitance. Budgeted battery life from average current, totaling ~2.1 Ah over 150 days against ~3 Ah from lithium cells rated to −40 °C.

Alternative design
Designed an alternative thermal imaging approach around an MLX90640 32×24 thermopile array, calculating a 27.4 cm mounting distance from the sensor's field of view and estimating ~1 year of battery life on one 18650 cell with deep-sleep duty cycling.

Handing it over
Wrote a step-by-step build guide and a net-by-net wiring reference so club members with no soldering experience could build, test, and install the monitor.

title: Embedded Systems Intern
summary: Cut load-cell noise from ±1 g to ±50 mg, drew a full transmitter schematic, and assembled 100+ boards.
details:
RC transmitter schematics
Drew Altium schematics for an internal RC aircraft transmitter (ESP32, RYLR993 LoRa module, USB-to-SPI joystick bridge), building every symbol and footprint from scratch with JLCPCB part numbers for direct BOM ordering.

Load cell dispenser
Wired the load cell and wrote the firmware for a stepper-driven dispenser that dispenses by weight, testing NAU7802 and HX711 24-bit ADCs. Reduced noise from ±1 g to ±50 mg by proposing an LDO supply, which halved the noise on its own, then moving the decoupling caps to the ADC pins and enabling the PGA filter cap on the unused channel.

Board assembly
Assembled 100+ boards for a medical project using stencil paste reflow and hand soldering, then tested each one and fixed any shorted rails, cold joints, or reversed diodes.

title: Size-Targeted JPEG Compression
summary: Modified JPEG so you set the output file size instead of a quality level; predicted size within 5.6% on average.
details:
The idea
Modified JPEG so the user sets the output file size instead of a quality level, using Lagrange multipliers to choose the quantization table scale and zero-rounding threshold that minimize mean squared error at that size.

Predicting file size
Developed an original file size estimation method by modeling DCT coefficients with a Laplacian distribution and deriving the average Huffman code length from the ITU-T T.81 tables, predicting compressed size within 5.6% on average across 5 test images.

Making it run
Cut MATLAB solver runtime from failing to finish overnight to 2.6 s by factoring the symbolic variables out of million-term sums.

Write-up
Wrote up the full method and results in a ~4,000-word research report, with guidance from a mathematics mentor.

title: School AI Backend
summary: A study assistant backend built with an AI coding assistant; I use it dozens of times a day.
details:
What it is
Built on my own with an AI coding assistant: a FastAPI service that syncs student-visible Canvas course content, indexes it for retrieval, and serves it to a Custom GPT, with every result carrying its source URL. I use it dozens of times a day.

Syncing and search
Each sync treats Canvas as a graph, recording links between resources, versioning changed content and chunking it for search. Search combines an English full-text (tsvector) index with exact pgvector cosine similarity in PostgreSQL. Syncs are idempotent, using canonical resource keys and content hashes, and only transient errors are retried.

Deployment and testing
It runs as a stateless, non-root Docker container on Google Cloud Run with secrets in Secret Manager, with Cloud Scheduler running incremental syncs every 4 hours and a full sync daily. It also handles Google Calendar operations with validation and audit rows. I wrote pytest unit tests for pagination, link discovery, calendar validation, chunking and auth.

title: CNC Programmer
summary: Programmed and ran CNC cuts for 3 whole-house and 5+ smaller cabinetry projects, over $100K CAD.
details:
CNC programming
Programmed and ran CNC cuts in Mozaik CAD/CAM from architectural drawings for 3 whole-house and 5+ smaller projects (over $100K CAD), often working alone in the shop, where any cutting error meant wasted material, rework, and missed install deadlines.

Parametric templates
Built parametric cabinet templates driven by algebraic constraints that adjust in all three dimensions to customer specifications, eliminating manual recalculation on every order.

Catching errors
Caught incorrect measurements and tool geometries in G-code that appeared correct in the renderings and shop drawings, along with cutting blade issues, before they reached production.

Nesting and lighting
Optimized part nesting to minimize offcut waste and planned under-cabinet LED lighting against residential electrical drawings.

title: Clip-On Tablet Stand
summary: A 3D-printed stand that clips onto a keyboard so a tablet can replace a laptop.
details:
Design
I modeled a tablet stand in Autodesk Fusion around a photo of the keyboard, and 3D printed it on my own printer. To save time and filament, I fit tested with narrow printed strips before printing the full part.

Locking mechanism
I also designed a locking mechanism with friction-fit blocks that attaches to a separate adjustable stand. I built and used it as a laptop replacement.

title: Creation of Custom Keyboard and Data Cable
summary: Soldered and assembled a functional keyboard and accompanying cable.
details:
Planning
Responsible for planning, purchasing and assembling parts.

Build
Build process involved manual lubrication and soldering of switches, as well as cutting, wrapping, and soldering the cable.
